title: Brazilian lime mousse (mousse de limão)
summary: A sharp, airy lime mousse that keeps the tang of the Brazilian classic, made with cream, cream cheese and allulose in place of condensed milk.
steps: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water and leave 5 minutes to swell, then melt it by warming 10–15 seconds in the microwave or over hot water. Do not let it boil.
Beat the cream cheese with the powdered erythritol and allulose until completely smooth. Beat in the lime juice a little at a time, then the zest, salt and melted gelatin.
In a separate cold bowl whip the cream to soft peaks.
Stir a third of the cream into the lime mixture to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest until no streaks remain.
Spoon into six glasses and chill at least 3 hours, until set. Finish with a little grated lime zest.

swaps.note: chill the can overnight and whip only the thick part

dairy_free_notes: Whipped coconut cream holds less air than dairy cream, so the mousse is denser and the coconut flavour sits alongside the lime; the gelatin is what keeps it set.
tips: In the original, the acid in the lime juice thickens the condensed milk on its own; without condensed milk the gelatin does that job.
Zest the limes before juicing them, and avoid the bitter white pith.

origin.history: Mousse de limão is one of Brazil's most familiar home desserts, built on sweetened condensed milk, cream and the juice and zest of limes. Condensed milk became a mainstay of Brazilian sweets during the twentieth century, and this quick, no-bake mousse is a product of that kitchen; it has no single recorded inventor.
